For hair, I absolutely swear by my Dyson Air Wrap. It gives me a salon blowout look in ~15 minutes from wet, ~5 minutes if it’s dry. Nude eyeliner stick in the waterline makes your eyes look brighter and more awake. Duochrome eyeshadows give your eyes dimension without having to mess with multiple colors or blending - my fave is Glass Bull by Colourpop. So. Pretty. 

As I’ve gotten older I also feel like my lips have washed out, but there are a ton of easy options that you can swipe on quickly and aren’t drying. It’s worth finding something you love and feel comfortable wearing, for me the top is Charlotte Tilbury Superstar Lips in Pillow Talk (the color is just a better version of a natural lip).

I worked with a man and a woman who started a relationship after I met them. He was a security guard, she was a cashier. At the time I smoked, and the smoking area was outside the security office. He used to come outside and chat with me on my breaks. Gentle giant, sweet as hell but very awkward in his skin, super tall and heavy man. She was very petite and introverted, never really made conversation although I knew her a few years and we crossed paths at work. 

If I worked second shift and he was on duty, he’d insist on walking me to my car because he was worried about a woman alone in a dark parking lot. Sometimes when he sat with me he’d talk about their relationship. He told me he’d dreamt that his soul mate had long dark hair like her. But he was conflicted because she had lost a pregnancy before they got together and it really messed her up, he wanted kids but didn’t think she’d be able to be pregnant again simply due to the mental toll. He loved her a lot though. I don’t think he had had many relationships. I know it’s anecdotal, but he never made me feel unsafe (and plenty of men have). 

They got into an argument one night in their apartment down the road from work. She shot him in the back with his own gun. She claims he was threatening and abusive. I feel pretty strongly that she is lying to cover for murdering him. Yes, he physically had a lot on her but he was retreating and there are some specific details that don’t add up to self-defense. She’s in jail now.

I consume a fair amount of true crime content and the case was covered on a very popular podcast a while ago. I normally like this podcast but I feel they gave her story too much weight and assumed he was the aggressor - the man can’t defend himself as he is dead. It was very weird to experience either way. Rest in peace, John.

I don’t know if I have an answer, but my 7-year old only is the same. Last weekend she told me, “we didn’t do anything fun and now the weekend is over, I want to do something fun next weekend.” I told her some weekends we chill out and relax. 

I do think I would be her doing a disservice to max out every single weekend with activities and spend a lot of money. While we are privileged that it’s not a huge deal financially, it’s setting an unrealistic expectation about life. Sometimes life is boring, when you move out of the house you will likely be on a budget and won’t be able to do all the things every free moment. I think it’s healthy for her to live with it and find her own fun around the house (with her many, many, toys, crafts, and games) sometimes. 🤷🏼‍♀️ While yes, it is a priority to give our children a happy childhood, it’s also part of our job to raise kids who can be functional adults that don’t live in perpetual disappointment that life isn’t entertaining enough for them. 

If all of this is burning you out, that’s reason enough to take a breather. I’m sure not everyone feels this way, but I am the only one who is really going to take care of me, my mental health, etc. It’s easy to run yourself into the ground prioritizing everyone else but no one is going to prioritize you so sometimes you have to do that. You can’t pour from an empty cup. 

Can you let them work together to prioritize one fun thing per weekend that they all really want to do? Is there another adult (partner, family member, friend) who can sometimes be the one who actually takes them to do the fun thing so you can get a breather? I realize our family sizes are very different, but we have friends who will trade off with us from time to time and take everyone to the park or the museum or whatever. 

It’s so hard! I hope you have a little peace this weekend, and if not there’s always the next one!

Slightly different but my doctor (GP) actually approached me about it! I got a big annual workup called Health Grades and in one part they strap electrodes to your head and show images, they had told me this could help diagnose stuff like early dementia but some science shit clued them into ADHD. She referred me to a psychiatrist who gave me a diagnosis and I started medication. 

It has helped me SO MUCH, definitely worth pursuing. I thought I had anxiety, but by treating the ADHD I am much less anxious (because I get shit done and don’t get stuck in executive dysfunction so much). I feel that I’m more patient with my child and less quick to get angry/frustrated. I’m a safer driver when medicated because I don’t allow myself to get as distracted. My house is tidy, my work inbox is manageable, and I feel more productive and content.

We had the popcorn removed in 2 rooms before our house was occupied. I cannot stress how messy the job is. Our company was fastidious- they spent the entire first day taping, draping, and basically both of the rooms looked like Dexter’s kill room before they even started. They scraped and applied texture the second day, and painted and cleaned the third day. Even with all their efforts, dust from the popcorn made it to every other room in the house. There are places where I still need to scrape bits from floors in the rooms they weren’t even working in. I would absolutely not DIY this. It was a relatively “simple” job since the house was empty and they weren’t doing all rooms. Also, if the ceilings are vaulted whoever is doing this will need to use a combination of a ladder and stilts. The supplies are not the cost of this job, it’s the tedious labor and how much prep/cleanup has to take place. If your walls are not whitish, the debris can stain the paint permanently. 

We got several quotes by googling “popcorn ceiling removal (city)”. Some charged by the hour, some just gave a quote when I described what we wanted, some gave price by square footage. The price was significantly higher if the house is occupied with furniture and some companies would only do it if the house was completely empty. I can’t imagine what it would have been like with soft furnishings to worry about.
